policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV renders 'in his sight': third-person suffix matches the ketiv בעינו; the qere בְּעֵינַי would be 'in my sight'.
ASV 'his apparel' is a collective noun that renders either the plural qere שִׂמְלֹתָיו or the singular ketiv שמלתו; no note is mapped to this unit.

ASV 'will be gracious to me' renders the verb identically whether it is the weqatal qere וְחַנַּנִי or the yiqtol ketiv יחנני; the waw of the qere is conjugational and leaves no English trace, and no note is mapped.

ASV text reads 'he called his name Solomon', the masculine ketiv ויקרא; the mapped textual_variant note 'Another reading is, she called' records the feminine qere וַתִּקְרָא as the alternative not adopted.

ASV 'brickkiln' (note: 'Or, brick-mould') renders מַלְבֵּן, the qere; the ketiv במלכן is not a word for brickkiln. The 'slight change in the Hebrew text' note concerns the verb 'made them pass through'/'made them labor', not this noun.
